newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK December manufacturing output.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK December manufacturing output.

text.p: Following is a selection of reactions to data showing UK manufacturing output rose 0.2 pct m/m and 1.4 pct y/y in December, while industrial production was up 0.6 pct m/m and 1.9 pct y/y.
The consensus forecast was 0.3% m/m, 1.1% y/y for manufacturing output, 0.5% m/m, 1.3% y/y industrial production.
"Not strong enough to change the interest rate argument much in favour of the Governor."

"I think we can confidently expect nothing on rates now. Clarke will take a lot of persuading before the election now. It doesn't look as though the increase in demand is reaching the industrial production numbers."

"The 1995 December figure was very weak, so a small uptick in the month on month figure has produced a good year on year figure. But it does show that manufacturing remains relatively weak in the UK at the moment compared to the overall position in the economy...Industrial production is going to have to go a lot higher than this to push the Governor's argument for an interest rate rise. I think we will see an increase in industrial production because the rest of the economy, the services sector, is growing quite strongly and there is still plenty of demand, with incomes rising and wages rising at reasonably rates."

"Broad picture is still one of moderate growth in manufacturing, with the trend dampened somewhat by ongoing efforts to reduce stocks. Inventories are now lean, however, so if domestic demand picks up as anticipated, output should similarly accelerate over coming months. Data confirm that it is the service sector that is currently leading the upswing, but we should look for the goods producing sector to begin to narrow the gap before long. Data soft enough to allow the chancellor to maintain a steady rate policy near term at least. Odds still very much in favour of no rate hike this side of the election."
